dstask

Single binary terminal-based TODO manager with git-based sync + markdown notes per task




Dstask is a personal task tracker designed to help you focus. It is similar to [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) but uses git to synchronise instead of a special protocol. If you're at home in the terminal, and with solving the occasional merge conflict, then dstask is for you! https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/589d06fd-7486-46e4-b838-ce85af12f0fc [Video courtesy of xGoivo -- thanks!](https://www.reddit.com/r/taskwarrior/comments/1o7itzg/what_do_you_guys_think_about_this_taskwarrior/) ## Features - Powerful context system (automatically applies filter/tags to queries and new tasks) - **Git powered sync**/undo/resolve ([passwordstore.org](https://www.passwordstore.org/) style) which means no need to set up a sync server, and syncing between devices is easy! - Task listing won't break with long task text - `note` command -- edit a **full markdown note** for each task. **Checklists are useful here.** - `open` command -- **open URLs found in specified task** (including notes) in the browser - zsh/bash completion (including tags and projects in current context) for speed; PowerShell completion on Windows - A single statically-linked binary - import tool which can import GitHub issues or taskwarrior tasks. ## Non-features - Collaboration. This is a personal task tracker. Use another system for projects that involve multiple people. Note that it can still be beneficial to use dstask to track what you are working on in the context of a multi-person project tracked elsewhere. ## Requirements - Git - A 256-color capable terminal ## Installation 1. Copy the executable (from the [releases page][releases]) to somewhere in your PATH. - Linux/macOS: name it `dstask` and mark it executable (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/`). - Windows: use `dstask.exe` and place it in a directory on `PATH` (e.g. `%USERPROFILE%\bin`). 1. Enable shell completions: - Bash: add `source <(dstask bash-completion)` to your `.bashrc`. - Zsh: add `dstask zsh-completion > /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_dstask` or source completions in your `~/.zshrc`. - PowerShell (Windows): see section "PowerShell completion" below. 1. Set up an alias in your `.bashrc`: `alias task=dstask` or `alias t=dstask` to make task management slightly faster. 1. Create or clone a `~/.dstask` git repository for the data, if you haven't already: - Linux/macOS: `mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init` - Windows: `mkdir %USERPROFILE%\.dstask && git -C %USERPROFILE%\.dstask init` ## PowerShell completion Save the completion script to a file and source it in your PowerShell profile: ```powershell dstask powershell-completion > ~\Documents\WindowsPowerShell\dstask-completion.ps1 Add-Content $PROFILE '. ~/Documents/WindowsPowerShell/dstask-completion.ps1' ``` ## Usage Run `dstask help` for usage information. ### Basic Commands - `dstask add [tags] [project:name] [priority:P0-P3]` - Add a new task - `dstask` or `dstask next` - Show next tasks to work on - `dstask start` - Start working on a task - `dstask stop` - Stop working on a task - `dstask done` - Mark a task as complete - `dstask edit` - Edit a task - `dstask note` - Edit the markdown note for a task - `dstask open` - Open URLs in task and note - `dstask show-open` - Show all open tasks - `dstask show-resolved` - Show completed tasks - `dstask show-paused` - Show paused tasks - `dstask context ` - Switch to a context (filter) - `dstask sync` - Synchronise with git remote ### Task Properties - **Priority**: P0 (highest), P1, P2 (default), P3 (lowest) - **Tags**: Add with `+tag`, remove with `-tag` - **Projects**: Set with `project:name` - **Due dates**: Set with `due:YYYY-MM-DD` - **Status**: open, active, paused, resolved ### Contexts Contexts automatically filter tasks and apply tags to new tasks: ```bash dstask context work dstask add finish report # automatically tagged with +work dstask # shows only work tasks dstask context -- # clear context ``` ### Git Sync Sync your tasks across devices using git: ```bash # Set up sync on first device cd ~/.dstask git remote add origin git push -u origin master # On other devices git clone ~/.dstask # To sync dstask sync 9940 characters elided texts for different areas of your life (work, home, etc.) to maintain focus. - Use tags liberally to categorize tasks, but avoid tag explosion. Use 3-5 tags per task at most. - Keep task summaries brief. Use the note field for details, checklists, and context. - Use dstask to track things you might forget, rather than everything. SNR is important. Don't track tasks for the sake of it, and don't track _ideas_. Track ideas separately. - Spend regular time reviewing tasks. You'll probably find some you've already resolved, and many you've forgotten. The `show-unorganised` command is good for this. - Try to work through tasks from the top of the list. Dstask sorts by priority then creation date -- the most important tasks are at the top. - Use `start`/`stop` to mark what you're genuinely working on right now; it makes resuming work faster. Paused tasks will be slightly highlighted, so you won't lose track of them. `show-paused` helps if they start to pile up. - Keep a [github-style check list](https://help.github.com/en/articles/about-task-lists) in the markdown note of complex or procedural tasks - Failing to get started working? Start with the smallest task - Record only required tasks. Track ideas separately, else your task list will grow unboundedly! - set `DSTASK_CONTEXT` in a `.envrc` per-project repository. With direnv, this allows you to automatically switch context ## Database The default database location is: - Linux/macOS: `~/.dstask/` - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.dstask` It can be configured by the environment variable `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`. ## Integration of fuzzy finders Instead of passing task IDs to commands, a fuzzy finder like [*fzf*](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf) can be used to search tasks by their summary instead. This is not part of dstask itself, but can be achieved by defining a shell wrapper like this in your `.bashrc` or `.zshrc`: ```bash function dstask () { local has_double_dash subcommand if (( $# == 1 || $# == 2 )); then has_double_dash="$( [[ "$1" == "--" || "$2" == "--" ]] && echo "1" || echo "0" )" subcommand="$( [[ "$1" == "--" ]] && echo "$2" || echo "$1" )" if (( $# == 1 || has_double_dash )) && \ [[ "${subcommand}" =~ ^(done|edit|note|open|remove|start|stop)$ ]] then command dstask show-open $( (( has_double_dash )) && echo "--" ) \ | jq -r '.[] | [.id, .summary] | @tsv' \ | fzf --delimiter='\t' --nth=2 --accept-nth=1 --preview='DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1 dstask {1} --' \ | xargs -n1 dstask "${subcommand}" return fi fi command dstask "$@" } ``` The wrapper function checks if dstask was called with a subcommand missing the task ID, and if so uses the `show-open` command to get a list of tasks to choose from. `--` can be used to ignore the current context for the fuzzy search. All other commands are passed directly to dstask. ## Alternatives Alternatives listed must be capable of running in the terminal. - [TaskLite](https://github.com/ad-si/TaskLite) -- The CLI task manager for power users, written in Haskell - [Taskwarrior](https://taskwarrior.org/) -- the closest analogue - [Taskbook](https://github.com/klaussinani/taskbook) -- board metaphor, note support - [todo.txt-cli](https://github.com/todotxt/todo.txt-cli) - [etm](https://github.com/dagraham/etm-dgraham) -- event and task manager - [t](https://github.com/sjl/t) -- a minimal todo list with an amusing philosophy ## FAQ > Does dstask encrypt tasks? Encryption is not a design goal of dstask. If you want to have your remote repository encrypted, you may consider [git-remote-gcrypt](https://spwhitton.name/tech/code/git-remote-gcrypt/) or [git-crypt](https://github.com/AGWA/git-crypt). Note that dstask has not been tested with these tools, nor can any claims be made about the security of the tools themselves. > Is it possible to modify more than one task at once with a filter? Yes. 1. Set a context: 2. Run a modify command without and ID 3. Hit y to confirm to modify all tasks in context This means it's natural to review the tasks that would be modified before modifying by listing all tasks in the current context first, instead of potentially operating blindly by matching tags or numbers. You can also specify multiple task numbers at one time, as with any other command. > Is there a GUI or web interface? Not as part of dstask itself. However, dstask can be used as a library -- @botto has started developing a web GUI, specifically to allow task management on-the-go via a smartphone: . It's in early stages but is meaningful as having no smartphone-based control is a blocker for a lot of people. > Has dstask been featured in a magazine? Yes! :-) [releases]: https://github.com/naggie/dstask/releases .: LICENSE README.md doc executable ./doc: dstask-import.md taskwarrior-migration.md

# dstask-import

usage: `dstask-import github|tw`

dstask-import is a tool to synchronize between external services or tools, and dstask.
At this point it supports importing from:

* taskwarrior
* GitHub

See below for details on each

## Taskwarrior

The import functionality is designed to aid with the transition from using taskwarrior to dstask.

Before installing dstask, you may want to export your taskwarrior database:

    task export > taskwarrior.json

After un-installing taskwarrior and installing dstask, to import the tasks to
dstask after initialising the dstask database with git:

    mkdir ~/.dstask && git -C ~/.dstask init
    dstask-import tw < taskwarrior.json

Note that the import process is lossy due to subtle differences between taskwarrior and dstask.

## GitHub

You can import issues from GitHub repositories into dstask.

### Authentication

To import from private repositories, you'll need a GitHub personal access token.
For public repositories, authentication is optional but recommended to avoid rate limits.

### Usage

To import issues from a GitHub repository:

    dstask-import github <owner>/<repo>

You can also import from multiple repositories by running the command multiple times.

# Moving from Taskwarrior

## Importing data

Please see the [dstask-import tw instructions](dstask-import.md#taskwarrior) to import taskwarrior tasks.

## Using dstask

Commands and syntax are deliberately very similar to taskwarrior. Here are the exceptions:

  * The command is (nearly) always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will. If there's an ID, it can proceed the command but doesn't have to.
  * Priorities are added by the keywords `P0` `P1` `P2` `P3`. Lower number is more urgent. Default is `P2`. For example `task add eat some bananas P1`. The keyword can be anywhere after the command.
  * Action is always the first argument. Eg, `task eat some add bananas` won't work, but `task add eat some bananas` will.
  * Contexts are defined on-the-fly, and are added to all new tasks if set. Use `--` to ignore current context in any command.

{"command":"rm -rf ~/.dstask
ls -la ~
python3 - << 'PY'
import subprocess, os, tempfile, pathlib, json, sys, textwrap
# helper to explore systematically, saving to /tmp/out.txt
PY
# set up isolated env
cat > /tmp/env.sh <<'EOS'
export TESTDIR=$(mktemp -d)
export HOME=$TESTDIR/home
mkdir -p $HOME
export DSTASK_GIT_REPO=$TESTDIR/repo
mkdir -p $DSTASK_GIT_REPO
git -C $DSTASK_GIT_REPO init -q
git -C $DSTASK_GIT_REPO config user.email "t@t.com"
git -C $DSTASK_GIT_REPO config user.name "Test"
export TERM=xterm-256color
EOS
source /tmp/env.sh; echo $TESTDIR; echo $DSTASK_GIT_REPO > /tmp/repo_path; echo $HOME > /tmp/home_path; echo $TESTDIR > /tmp/testdir_path
./executable next 2>&1; echo EXIT:$?
ls -la $DSTASK_GIT_REPO
cat $DSTASK_GIT_REPO/* 2>/dev/null | head
"}

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def fresh():
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(); home=os.path.join(td,"home"); os.makedirs(home); repo=os.path.join(td,"repo"); os.makedirs(repo)
    subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"init","-q"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.email","t@t.com"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.name","T"])
    return td,home,repo
def run(home,repo,*a,env=None,inp=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo)
    if env: e.update(env)
    p=subprocess.run([EXE]+list(a),capture_output=True,text=True,env=e,input=inp)
    print(a, p.returncode, repr(p.stdout[:200]), repr(p.stderr[:200]), "dirs:", sorted(os.listdir(repo)))
    return p

for cmd in ["next","show-open","show-tags","show-projects","context","help","version","bash-completion","git"]:
    td,home,repo=fresh()
    args=[cmd] if cmd!="git" else [cmd,"status"]

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from h import *

def idsbin():
    import pathlib, subprocess

run(home,repo,"add","a"); idsbin()

run(home,repo,"show-resolved"); run(home,repo,"show-open")
run(home,repo,"add","c"); idsbin()
# remove ids file manually
import os

run(home,repo,"show-open"); idsbin()
run(home,repo,"show-resolved")
# remove then undo
run(home,repo,"2","remove"); idsbin(); gitlog(repo)
run(home,repo,"undo"); idsbin(); run(home,repo,"show-open")
# resolve then undo
run(home,repo,"1","done"); run(home,repo,"undo"); run(home,repo,"show-open"); idsbin()
# delete a file manually, add
import glob
for f in glob.glob(repo+"/pending/*.yml"): print(f, open(f).read())

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from h import *
import os
fake={"DSTASK_FAKE_PTY":"1"}
cases = [
 ("status active", "s/status: pending/status: active/"),
 ("status paused", "s/status: pending/status: paused/"),
 ("status template", "s/status: pending/status: template/"),
 ("status bogus", "s/status: pending/status: bogus/"),
 ("status empty", "s/status: pending/status:/"),
 ("priority bogus", "s/priority: P2/priority: PX/"),
 ("priority empty", "s/priority: P2/priority:/"),
 ("summary empty", "s/summary: orig/summary:/"),
 ("summary spaces", "s/summary: orig/summary: ' '/"),
 ("created changed", "s/created: .*/created: 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z/"),
 ("resolved set", "s/resolved: .*/resolved: 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z/"),
 ("due changed", "s|due: .*|due: 2020-02-03T00:00:00Z|"),
 ("uuid added", "1i uuid: myuuid"),
 ("id added", "1i id: 99"),
 ("extra field", "1i extra: hi"),
 ("tags string", "s/tags: \\[\\]/tags: notalist/"),
 ("tags removed line", "/^tags:/d"),
 ("notes multiline", "s/notes: \"\"/notes: 'line1\\nline2'/"),
]
# orig task creation has tags [] etc; need sed patterns adapted: add has no notes etc file generated by editor - inspect patterns fine
for label, expr in cases:
    td,home,repo=fresh()
    run(home,repo,"add","orig")

    print("Edited file content:", open(td+"/edited.txt").read() if os.path.exists(td+"/edited.txt") else "?")

    run(home,repo,"show-templates")

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from h import *
import os
fake={"DSTASK_FAKE_PTY":"1"}
td,home,repo=fresh()
run(home,repo,"template","templ task")
run(home,repo,"add","pendingtask")
for cmd in [["1","start"],["1","stop"],["1","done"],["1","remove"],["1","note","x"],["1","edit"],["1","open"],["1","modify","+x"],["2","start"],["2","stop"],["2","done"]]:
    env=fake if cmd[-1] in ("edit",) or "note" in cmd else None
    # note fake needed to append; edit need editor cat
    extra={}
    if "edit" in cmd: extra={"EDITOR":"cat"}
    run(home,repo,*cmd,env={**(fake if "note" in cmd or "edit" in cmd else {}),**extra},inp="n\n")
    run(home,repo,"show-templates"); run(home,repo,"show-open")
PY

add("Beta thing","+red","project:api","P0")
add("gamma","banana","+green","P3")
add("Delta banana","+blue","project:web","P2","due:2026-06-01")
run(home,repo,"2","start")

 [],["alpha"],["ALPHA"],["banana"],["bananas"],["notes"],["+red"],["+RED"],["-red"],["+red","+blue"],["+red","-blue"],["project:web"],["project:WEB"],["-project:web"],["-project:api"],["P1"],["P0","P1"],["due:2025-06-01"],["due:2025-06-02"],["+red","beta"],["beta","+red"],["beta","gamma"],["1"],["2"],["1","2"],["99"],["0"],["-1"],["+red","--"],["--","+red"],["project:web","alpha"],["due:today"],["P2"],["x"]
]
for f in filters:
    for cmd in ["next","show-open"]:
        p=run(home,repo,cmd,*f)
        if p.returncode==0:
            ids=[x['id'] for x in json.loads(p.stdout)]
            print(cmd,f,"ids",ids)
        else:
            print(cmd,f,"ERR",p.returncode,p.stderr)
# show commands with filters
for cmd in ["show-active","show-paused","show-resolved","show-templates","show-unorganised","show-tags","show-projects"]:
    for f in [[],["+red"],["banana"],["project:web"],["--"]]:
        p=run(home,repo,cmd,*f)
        print("SHOW",cmd,f,p.returncode,repr(p.stdout[:500]),repr(p.stderr[:200]))
PY
cat /tmp/filter.txt

{"command":"python3 - << 'PY'
import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from h import *
for inp in ["y\n","n\n","\n","yes\n","Y\n",None,""]:
    td,home,repo=fresh()
    run(home,repo,"add","alpha")
    run(home,repo,"add","beta")
    print("INPUT",repr(inp))
    if inp is None:
        # subprocess with stdin from devnull? Our run with inp=None inherits python stdin (heredoc EOF?) Let's pass /dev/null via custom
        import subprocess, os
        e=dict(os.environ); e.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo)
        p=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","modify","+z"],capture_output=True,text=True,env=e,stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        print(p.returncode,repr(p.stdout),repr(p.stderr))
    else:
        run(home,repo,"modify","+z",inp=inp)
    run(home,repo,"show-open")
PY
"}

def show(home,repo):
    p=run(home,repo,"show-open","--"); print([(x['id'],x['summary'],x['tags'],x['project'],x['priority']) for x in json.loads(p.stdout)])

run(home,repo,"modify","P0",inp="y\n")
show(home,repo)

show(home,repo)
run(home,repo,"context","none")

show(home,repo)
# in context, modify with ID outside context
run(home,repo,"context","+work")
run(home,repo,"2","modify","+outsider")
show(home,repo)
# in context, modify a task by ID - does context merge affect task attributes? e.g. modify priority while context priority etc
run(home,repo,"context","P1")
run(home,repo,"2","modify","+ctxtest")
show(home,repo)
PY
"}

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/workspace/executable"
def fresh():
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(); home=os.path.join(td,"home"); os.makedirs(home); repo=os.path.join(td,"repo"); os.makedirs(repo)
    subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"init","-q"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.email","t@t.com"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.name","T"])
    return td,home,repo
def q(home,repo,*a,env=None,inp=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo); e.pop("DSTASK_CONTEXT",None); e.pop("DSTASK_FAKE_PTY",None); e.pop("EDITOR",None)
    if env:
        for k,v in env.items():
            if v is None: e.pop(k,None)
            else: e[k]=v
    return subprocess.run([EXE]+list(a),capture_output=True,text=True,env=e,input=inp)

 "a.b/c",

        out+=d
    p.wait(); os.close(master)

# wire bash completions to dstask completion engine. Some of the workarounds for
# idiosyncrasies around separation with colons taken from /etc/bash_completion

_dstask() {
    # reconstruct COMP_WORDS to re-join separations caused by colon (which is a default separator)
    # yes, this method ends up splitting by spaces, but that's not a problem for the dstask parser
    # see http://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/FAQ
    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    # hand to dstask as canonical args
    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

complete -F _dstask dstask
complete -F _dstask task

td,home,repo=fresh(); q(home,repo,"add","Alpha task","+red","+blue","project:web","P1","due:2025-06-01","/","some notes"); q(home,repo,"add","Beta","+red","project:api","P0")
env={"HOME":home,"DSTASK_GIT_REPO":repo,"TERM":"xterm-256color"}

def widths_for(w):
    code,out=run_pty(["/workspace/executable","next"],width=w,height=20,env=env)
    lines=[strip(l) for l in out.decode().replace('\r','').split('\n')]
    # starts based on known row: use header line positions but truncated words hard. Use second row: values 2,P0,red,api,Beta positions and summary start known via Beta start.
    # Better infer column starts from header by scanning segments: columns separated by 2 spaces in header (but truncated values no trailing spaces for last).
    # Use positions of header tokens approximated with sequence search for column beginnings from row cells: ID row token positions: row tokens.
    lines=[l for l in lines if l.strip()]
    header=lines[0]
    # column starts are where header cell starts; can find by using row1: tokens but empty cells complicate.
    # We'll reconstruct widths from line length and token starts in header for first 5 fragments (each fragment begins col)
    frags=[m.start() for m in re.finditer(r'\S+',header)]
    # frags might be >6 if summary etc, first 6 are cols (Due has maybe)
    starts=frags[:5]+[frags[5] if len(frags)>5 else len(header)]
    # Actually Due column cell could be empty in header? It's word.
    widths=[]
    for i,s in enumerate(starts):
        if i<5: widths.append(starts[i+1]-s-2)
        else: widths.append(len(header)-s)
    return widths,header
for w in range(69,14,-1):
    widths,hdr=widths_for(w); print(w,widths)

import subprocess, os, tempfile
EXE="/tmp/testbin"
def fresh():
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(); home=os.path.join(td,"home"); os.makedirs(home); repo=os.path.join(td,"repo"); os.makedirs(repo)
    subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"init","-q"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.email","t@t.com"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.name","T"])
    return td,home,repo
def q(home,repo,*a,env=None,inp=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo); e.pop("DSTASK_CONTEXT",None); e.pop("DSTASK_FAKE_PTY",None); e.pop("EDITOR",None)
    if env:
        for k,v in env.items():
            if v is None: e.pop(k,None)
            else: e[k]=v
    return subprocess.run([EXE]+list(a),capture_output=True,text=True,env=e,input=inp)
PY

    original_args=( $(echo "${COMP_WORDS[@]}" | sed 's/ : /:/g' | sed 's/ :$/:/g') )

    COMPREPLY=( $(dstask _completions "${original_args[@]}") )

    # convert dstask's suggestions to remove prefix before colon so complete can understand it
    local last_arg="${original_args[-1]}"
    local colon_word=${last_arg%"${last_arg##*:}"}
    local i=${#COMPREPLY[*]}
    while [[ $((--i)) -ge 0 ]]; do
        COMPREPLY[$i]=${COMPREPLY[$i]#"$colon_word"}
    done
}

import sys, os, subprocess, re
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp'); from h2 import fresh as _fresh_orig
from ptyrun2 import run_pty
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; NEW="/tmp/testbin"
def setup(exe):
    import tempfile
    td=tempfile.mkdtemp(); home=os.path.join(td,"home"); os.makedirs(home); repo=os.path.join(td,"repo"); os.makedirs(repo)
    subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"init","-q"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.email","t@t.com"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.name","T"])
    return td,home,repo
def q(exe,home,repo,*a,env=None):
    e=dict(os.environ); e.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo); e.pop("DSTASK_CONTEXT",None); e.pop("DSTASK_FAKE_PTY",None)
    if env: e.update(env)
    return subprocess.run([exe]+list(a),capture_output=True,text=True,env=e)
def norm(b,td):
    s=b.decode(errors='replace') if isinstance(b,bytes) else b
    s=s.replace(td,"TD")
    s=re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}','UUID',s,flags=re.I)
    s=re.sub(r'20\d\d-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d(\.\d+)?Z','TIME',s)
    s=re.sub(r'20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d(\.\d+)? \+0000 UTC','TIME',s)
    s=re.sub(r'\[master[^\]]*\]','[master HASH]',s)
    return s
def compare_pty(name, setup_cmds, tests):
    outs=[]
    for exe in [ORIG,NEW]:
        td,home,repo=setup(exe)
        for a in setup_cmds: q(exe,home,repo,*a)
        res=[]
        env={"HOME":home,"DSTASK_GIT_REPO":repo,"TERM":"xterm-256color"}
        for args,w,h in tests:
            code,out=run_pty([exe]+args,width=w,height=h,env=env)
            res.append((args,w,h,code,norm(out,td)))
        outs.append(res)
    if outs[0]==outs[1]: print("OK",name)
    else:
        print("DIFF",name)
        for x,y in zip(*outs):
            if x!=y: print(" ORIG",x,"\n NEW",y)

    return s

        ed=os.path.join(td,"editor.py"); open(ed,"w").write("#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport sys\np=sys.argv[1]\ns=open(p).read()\n"+editor_body+"\nopen(p,'w').write(s)\n"); os.chmod(ed,0o755)
        logf=os.path.join(td,"editor.log")
        outs=[]
        for args,inp in cmds:
            p=run(exe,home,repo,*args,env={"DSTASK_FAKE_PTY":"1","EDITOR":ed},inp=inp); outs.append((args,p.returncode,norm(p.stdout,td),norm(p.stderr,td)))
        files=[]

            if '.git' in root: continue
            for f in fs:
                path=os.path.join(root,f); files.append((re.sub(r'[0-9a-f-]{36}','UUID',os.path.relpath(path,repo)),norm(open(path).read(),td)))
        results.append((outs,sorted(files,key=lambda x:x[1])))
    if results[0]==results[1]: print("OK",name)
    else:
        print("DIFF",name); print(" ORIG",results[0]); print(" NEW",results[1])

import subprocess, os, tempfile, re
ORIG="/workspace/executable"; NEW="/tmp/testbin"
def norm(s,td):
    s=s.replace(td,"TD"); s=re.sub(r'[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}','UUID',s,flags=re.I); s=re.sub(r'20\d\d-\d\d-\d\dT\d\d:\d\d:\d\d(\.\d+)?Z','TIME',s); s=re.sub(r'2026/\d\d/\d\d \d\d:\d\d:\d\d','DATE',s); s=re.sub(r'\[master[^\]]*\]','[master HASH]',s)
    return s
def run_scenario(name, files, cmds):
    results=[]
    for exe in [ORIG,NEW]:
        td=tempfile.mkdtemp(); home=os.path.join(td,"home"); os.makedirs(home); repo=os.path.join(td,"repo"); os.makedirs(repo)
        subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"init","-q"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.email","t@t.com"]); subprocess.run(["git","-C",repo,"config","user.name","T"])
        for status,fname,content in files:
            d=os.path.join(repo,status); os.makedirs(d,exist_ok=True); open(os.path.join(d,fname),"w").write(content)
        env=dict(os.environ); env.update(HOME=home,DSTASK_GIT_REPO=repo)
        outs=[]
        for a in cmds:
            p=subprocess.run([exe]+a,capture_output=True,text=True,env=env); outs.append((a,p.returncode,norm(p.stdout,td),norm(p.stderr,td)))
        results.append(outs)
    print(("OK " if results[0]==results[1] else "DIFF ")+name)
    if results[0]!=results[1]: print(" ORIG",results[0],"\n NEW",results[1])
